items.english: My name is Maria.
items.portuguese: Meu nome é Maria.
items.note: Use "I am" (or "I'm") with the pronoun "I". Never say "I is" or "I are".

items.english: I am a student.
items.portuguese: Eu sou um estudante.
items.note: Use "a" before consonant sounds (a teacher) and "an" before vowel sounds (an engineer).

items.english: I am Brazilian.
items.portuguese: Eu sou brasileiro(a).
items.note: Nationalities are adjectives. "I am Brazilian" NOT "I am a Brazilian" (without article is more common).

items.english: This is a book.
items.portuguese: Isto é um livro.
items.note: Use "is" for singular things (it is, this is) and "are" for plural (these are, they are).

items.english: Are you a student?
items.portuguese: Você é estudante?
items.note: For yes/no questions, put the verb before the subject: "Are you...?" "Is she...?"

beginner-02-personal-pronouns.title: Lição 2: Pronomes Pessoais
beginner-02-personal-pronouns.skill: Aprender todos os pronomes de sujeito (I, you, he, she, it, we, they)

items.english: I like coffee.
items.portuguese: Eu gosto de café.
items.note: Subject pronouns come BEFORE the verb: I eat, She runs, They work.

items.english: Can you help me?
items.portuguese: Você pode me ajudar?
items.note: Object pronouns come AFTER the verb: Call me, Help her, Tell them.

items.english: My name is João.
items.portuguese: Meu nome é João.
items.note: Possessive adjectives come BEFORE nouns: my book, her car, their house.

items.english: I have a sister. She is younger than me.
items.portuguese: Eu tenho uma irmã. Ela é mais nova que eu.
items.note: Mix subject, object, and possessive pronouns naturally in sentences.

beginner-03-simple-present.title: Lição 3: Presente Simples
beginner-03-simple-present.skill: Formar frases afirmativas (I work, She works)

items.english: I drink coffee every morning.
items.portuguese: Eu bebo café toda manhã.
items.note: Add -s or -es to the verb for he/she/it: work→works, go→goes, watch→watches.

items.english: I don't eat meat.
items.portuguese: Eu não como carne.
items.note: Use DON'T (do not) for I/you/we/they. Use DOESN'T (does not) for he/she/it. The main verb stays in base form!

items.english: Do you speak English?
items.portuguese: Você fala inglês?
items.note: Start with DO/DOES + subject + base verb. For Wh- questions: Wh-word + do/does + subject + verb.

items.english: I always brush my teeth before bed.
items.portuguese: Eu sempre escovo os dentes antes de dormir.
items.note: Frequency adverbs go BEFORE the main verb but AFTER the verb "to be": I always work. / I am always happy.

items.english: I wake up at 6:30 and take a shower.
items.portuguese: Eu acordo às 6:30 e tomo banho.
items.note: Connect sentences with "then", "after that", "before": I wake up, then I take a shower.

items.english: I have a cat.
items.portuguese: Eu tenho um gato.
items.note: Use 'a' before consonant SOUNDS. Use 'an' before vowel SOUNDS. It's about the sound, not the letter!

items.english: The book you gave me is great.
items.portuguese: O livro que você me deu é ótimo.
items.note: Use 'the' when both speaker and listener know which specific thing you mean, or for unique things.

items.english: I love music.
items.portuguese: Eu amo música. (em geral)
items.note: No article for: general/abstract concepts, languages, meals, sports, and some places (school, work, home).

items.english: I exercise in the morning.
items.portuguese: Eu me exercito de manhã.
items.note: Some expressions have fixed article usage - memorize them as phrases!

items.english: I have two brothers.
items.portuguese: Eu tenho dois irmãos.
items.note: Numbers 1-12 are unique. 13-19 end in -teen. Tens (20,30...) end in -ty. Combine: twenty-one, thirty-five.

items.english: This is my first English class.
items.portuguese: Esta é minha primeira aula de inglês.
items.note: Most ordinals add -th (fourth, fifth). Exceptions: first (1st), second (2nd), third (3rd). Use for dates and order.

items.english: I need some help.
items.portuguese: Eu preciso de alguma ajuda.
items.note: SOME for affirmative, ANY for questions/negatives. MUCH for uncountable, MANY for countable nouns.

items.english: How much is this shirt?
items.portuguese: Quanto custa esta camisa?
items.note: For prices: "ten dollars" or "ten ninety-nine" ($10.99). Ask: "How much is/are...?" or "How much does it cost?"

items.english: I like chocolate.
items.portuguese: Eu gosto de chocolate.
items.note: LIKE + noun (I like coffee) OR LIKE + verb-ing (I like reading). Never 'I like to read' for general habits.

items.english: I don't like spicy food.
items.portuguese: Eu não gosto de comida apimentada.
items.note: DON'T LIKE is polite. HATE is strong. CAN'T STAND is very strong. Use verb-ing after these.

items.english: My favorite food is pizza.
items.portuguese: Minha comida favorita é pizza.
items.note: Use 'favorite' + noun OR 'prefer X to Y' for comparisons. 'Best' = superlative for opinions.

items.english: Do you like your job?
items.portuguese: Você gosta do seu trabalho?
items.note: Use 'Do you like...?' for yes/no. Use 'What kind of... do you like?' for open questions.

items.english: I am learning English right now.
items.portuguese: Eu estou aprendendo inglês agora.
items.note: Structure: Subject + am/is/are + verb-ING. I am, You/We/They are, He/She/It is.

items.english: I'm not feeling well today.
items.portuguese: Não estou me sentindo bem hoje.
items.note: Negative: am/is/are + NOT + verb-ing. Questions: Am/Is/Are + subject + verb-ing?

items.english: Right now I am practicing English.
items.portuguese: Agora eu estou praticando inglês.
items.note: Time markers: right now, at the moment, currently, today, this week. Use 'Look!' and 'Listen!' to draw attention.

items.english: I work at a bank. (routine) / I am working at home today. (temporary)
items.portuguese: Eu trabalho em um banco. / Estou trabalhando em casa hoje.
items.note: Simple Present = habits, routines, facts. Present Continuous = happening NOW, temporary situations.

beginner-08-cafe-ordering.title: Lição 8: Pedindo em uma Cafeteria
beginner-08-cafe-ordering.skill: Usar frases educadas: 'I would like...', 'Can I have...?'

items.english: I would like a large coffee, please.
items.portuguese: Eu gostaria de um café grande, por favor.
items.note: Polite order: 'I would like...' (formal) > 'Can I have...?' > 'I'll have...' (casual). Always add 'please'!

items.english: A large cappuccino with almond milk, please.
items.portuguese: Um cappuccino grande com leite de amêndoa, por favor.
items.note: Specify: size (small/medium/large) + drink + 'with' + extras. 'No' + item you don't want.

items.english: How much is a large latte?
items.portuguese: Quanto custa um latte grande?
items.note: 'How much is/are...?' for prices. 'Can I pay by...?' for payment method. 'Here you go' when giving money/card.

items.english: Excuse me, is this seat taken?
items.portuguese: Com licença, este lugar está ocupado?
items.note: 'Is this...?' to ask about availability. 'We're out of...' = sold out. 'Can I get...?' for extra requests.

items.english: My brother is tall and slim.
items.portuguese: Meu irmão é alto e magro.
items.note: Use 'is/are' for appearance: He IS tall. She IS beautiful. For age: 'in his/her 20s/30s/40s'.

items.english: My mother has long black hair.
items.portuguese: Minha mãe tem cabelo preto longo.
items.note: Use 'HAS' for hair and eyes: She HAS long hair. He HAS brown eyes. (Not 'is'!)

items.english: My best friend is very outgoing.
items.portuguese: Meu melhor amigo é muito extrovertido.
items.note: Personality uses 'is/are': She IS friendly. Add 'very', 'really', 'quite', 'a bit' for intensity.

items.english: What does your sister look like?
items.portuguese: Como é a aparência da sua irmã?
items.note: 'What does X look like?' = physical. 'What is X like?' = personality. 'Who does X look like?' = resemblance.

beginner-10-family.title: Lição 10: Família e Relacionamentos
beginner-10-family.skill: Aprender todo o vocabulário de membros da família

items.english: I have one brother and two sisters.
items.portuguese: Eu tenho um irmão e duas irmãs.
items.note: Possessive + family: MY mother, YOUR father, HIS sister. 'Older/younger than me' for age comparison.

items.english: My grandfather passed away last year.
items.portuguese: Meu avô faleceu ano passado.
items.note: Family from parent's side: uncle = parent's brother, aunt = parent's sister. Cousin = uncle/aunt's child.

items.english: My husband and I have been married for 10 years.
items.portuguese: Meu marido e eu somos casados há 10 anos.
items.note: 'In-law' = through marriage: mother-in-law (spouse's mother), brother-in-law (spouse's brother or sister's husband).

items.english: Do you have any brothers or sisters?
items.portuguese: Você tem irmãos ou irmãs?
items.note: 'Do you have...?' for questions. 'There are X people in my family.' 'We are close' = good relationship.

beginner-11-basic-questions.title: Lição 11: Perguntas Básicas
beginner-11-basic-questions.skill: Usar todas as palavras interrogativas corretamente

items.english: What is your favorite food?
items.portuguese: Qual é sua comida favorita?
items.note: WHAT asks about things/information. WHERE asks about places/location. Structure: Question word + auxiliary + subject + verb.

items.english: When is the meeting?
items.portuguese: Quando é a reunião?
items.note: WHEN asks about time/dates. WHO asks about people. 'Who' as subject doesn't need 'do/does': Who lives here?

items.english: Why are you learning English?
items.portuguese: Por que você está aprendendo inglês?
items.note: WHY asks for reasons (answer with 'because...'). HOW asks about manner, method, or state.

items.english: What kind of books do you read?
items.portuguese: Que tipo de livros você lê?
items.note: Combinations: What + noun (What time?), How + adjective (How old?), How + adverb (How often?).

beginner-12-telling-time.title: Lição 12: Dizendo as Horas e Horários
beginner-12-telling-time.skill: Dizer as horas usando o'clock, half past, quarter to/past

items.english: It's three o'clock.
items.portuguese: São três horas.
items.note: o'clock = exact hour. Half past = :30. Quarter past = :15. Quarter to = :45. Or use digital: 'ten fifteen'.

items.english: Excuse me, what time is it?
items.portuguese: Com licença, que horas são?
items.note: 'What time is it?' or 'Do you have the time?' to ask current time. 'What time does X...?' for schedules.

items.english: I wake up at 7 AM.
items.portuguese: Eu acordo às 7 da manhã.
items.note: AT for exact times (at 9:00). IN for parts of day/months/years. ON for days/dates.

items.english: I work from 9 to 5.
items.portuguese: Eu trabalho das 9 às 5.
items.note: 'From X to Y' for duration. 'I'm free at/after...' for availability. Use days with 'on' (on Monday).

items.english: The cat is in the box.
items.portuguese: O gato está na caixa.
items.note: IN = inside enclosed spaces and countries/cities. ON = on surfaces or on top of something. AT = specific points and locations.

items.english: The cat is under the bed.
items.portuguese: O gato está embaixo da cama.
items.note: UNDER = below something. BEHIND = at the back of something. IN FRONT OF = facing something or before it.

items.english: My house is next to the supermarket.
items.portuguese: Minha casa fica ao lado do supermercado.
items.note: NEXT TO = beside something, very close. BETWEEN = in the middle of two things. ACROSS FROM = on the opposite side.

items.english: The painting is above the sofa.
items.portuguese: O quadro está acima do sofá.
items.note: ABOVE = higher than something. BELOW = lower than something. OVER = from one side to the other, higher. THROUGH = from inside one side to the other.

items.english: Where is the bathroom?
items.portuguese: Onde fica o banheiro?
items.note: Use WHERE IS for singular items and WHERE ARE for plural items or people. Prepositions answer WHERE questions.

items.english: It is sunny today.
items.portuguese: Está ensolarado hoje.
items.note: Use "It is" or "It's" with weather adjectives. Weather is usually described with impersonal "it".

items.english: It is snowing in the south of Brazil.
items.portuguese: Está nevando no sul do Brasil.
items.note: Some weather expressions use "there is" for specific weather events. "It is" for general conditions.

items.english: Spring is my favorite season.
items.portuguese: A primavera é minha estação favorita.
items.note: Season names can be used with "the" (the spring, the summer) or without. Seasons tell us expected weather.

items.english: What is the weather like today?
items.portuguese: Como está o tempo hoje?
items.note: "What is the weather like?" is the standard way to ask about weather. "How is the weather?" is also common.

items.english: The temperature is 28 degrees Celsius.
items.portuguese: A temperatura é de 28 graus Celsius.
items.note: Use temperature with degrees. Celsius is common in Brazil. Adjectives like warm, cool, cold describe how temperature feels.

items.english: This dress is beautiful.
items.portuguese: Este vestido é bonito.
items.note: THIS/THESE for near you, THAT/THOSE for far away. THIS/THAT are singular, THESE/THOSE are plural.

items.english: How much is this shirt?
items.portuguese: Quanto custa esta camiseta?
items.note: Use "How much is/are" to ask about price. Brazil uses Real (R$). Numbers are essential for prices.

items.english: I want to buy a pair of shoes.
items.portuguese: Quero comprar um par de sapatos.
items.note: Shopping vocabulary includes clothing sizes, colors, and store locations. Questions are common in shopping.

items.english: Can I help you?
items.portuguese: Posso ajudá-lo?
items.note: Polite phrases are important when shopping. Questions start with question words or auxiliary verbs.

items.english: This shirt is cheaper than that one.
items.portuguese: Esta camiseta é mais barata que aquela.
items.note: Use comparative adjectives to compare. "This is..." vs "That is..." for comparison.

items.english: I like eating chicken and rice.
items.portuguese: Gosto de comer frango e arroz.
items.note: Food words can be countable (an apple, two oranges) or uncountable (rice, milk, water).

items.english: I have an orange.
items.portuguese: Tenho uma laranja.
items.note: Countable: use "a/an", "one/two/three", "How many?" Uncountable: use "some", "How much?"

items.english: Breakfast is my favorite meal.
items.portuguese: O café da manhã é minha refeição favorita.
items.note: Meal names are: breakfast, lunch, dinner (or supper). Time is expressed with "at" + time.

items.english: I love Brazilian food.
items.portuguese: Adoro comida brasileira.
items.note: Express preferences with "I like", "I love", "I prefer". Cooking verbs include "cook", "bake", "grill".

items.english: I would like the feijoada, please.
items.portuguese: Gostaria do feijão, por favor.
items.note: "I would like" is polite for ordering. "Can I have" is casual. "Would you like" asks what someone wants.

items.english: Turn left at the next street.
items.portuguese: Vire à esquerda na próxima rua.
items.note: Imperative form for directions: turn, go, stop, wait. These are command forms without a subject.

items.english: The store is near the bank.
items.portuguese: A loja fica perto do banco.
items.note: Landmarks help give directions. Use "near", "across from", "next to", "past", "in front of", "behind".

items.english: Excuse me, where is the station?
items.portuguese: Com licença, onde fica a estação?
items.note: Use "Where is...?", "How do I get to...?", "Is it far?" Polite phrases like "Excuse me" are important.

items.english: I take the bus to work every day.
items.portuguese: Pego o ônibus para o trabalho todos os dias.
items.note: Use "take" for public transport (bus, train, taxi). Use "ride" for bike/motorcycle. Use "drive" for cars.

items.english: Where is the nearest bus stop?
items.portuguese: Onde é o ponto de ônibus mais próximo?
items.note: Questions about public transport use "Where", "When", "How much". Statements use imperatives or polite requests.

beginner-18-health-and-body.title: Lição 18: Saúde e Partes do Corpo

items.english: My head hurts.
items.portuguese: Minha cabeça dói.
items.note: Body parts use "my", "your", "his", "her". Pain is expressed with "have a" + problem (have a headache).

items.english: I have strong arms.
items.portuguese: Tenho braços fortes.
items.note: Body parts are countable. Use "arm/hand/leg/foot". Pain uses "have a" + pain type.

items.english: I have a cold and a fever.
items.portuguese: Tenho um resfriado e febre.
items.note: "Have a" for temporary illnesses (cold, fever, flu). "Feel" for symptoms (sick, dizzy, tired).

items.english: I need to see a doctor.
items.portuguese: Preciso ver um médico.
items.note: Doctor conversations use "I have", "I need", "I feel". Doctor uses imperatives: take, rest, come back.

items.english: I exercise every morning.
items.portuguese: Faço exercício toda manhã.
items.note: Health habits use imperatives (sleep more, eat healthy) or present simple (I exercise, I feel healthy).

items.english: I like reading books in the evening.
items.portuguese: Gosto de ler livros à noite.
items.note: Hobbies use "like/enjoy/love" + verb-ing (reading, painting). Or use "play" for instruments/games.

items.english: I play soccer with my friends.
items.portuguese: Jogo futebol com meus amigos.
items.note: "Play" for team sports (soccer, tennis, basketball). "Do" for activities (yoga, karate). "Go" for water sports.

items.english: I like playing video games.
items.portuguese: Gosto de jogar videogames.
items.note: Indoor activities commonly use "like/enjoy" + verb-ing. Can also use "play" for games and "watch" for movies/TV.

items.english: I love going hiking on weekends.
items.portuguese: Adoro fazer trilhas nos fins de semana.
items.note: "Go" + verb-ing for outdoor activities (go hiking, go camping, go fishing). Can also use "like + verb-ing".

items.english: What is your favorite hobby?
items.portuguese: Qual é seu hobby favorito?
items.note: Questions: "What is your hobby?", "Do you like...?", "What do you do...?" Answers: "I like...", "My hobby is...", "I prefer..."

beginner-20-clothes-and-fashion.title: Lição 20: Roupas e Moda
beginner-20-clothes-and-fashion.skill: Nomear peças de roupa em inglês

items.english: I am wearing a blue shirt.
items.portuguese: Estou vestindo uma camiseta azul.
items.note: Clothing nouns are countable: a shirt, a dress, pants (always plural), a hat. Use "wear" and "have".

items.english: I prefer white shirts.
items.portuguese: Prefiro camisetas brancas.
items.note: Color adjectives come before the noun: a blue shirt, red pants, yellow shoes. Most colors are singular.

items.english: He wears a formal suit to work.
items.portuguese: Ele usa um traje formal para o trabalho.
items.note: Clothing types follow noun rules. Some are countable (a suit, a shirt), some always plural (jeans, shorts).

items.english: What are you wearing today?
items.portuguese: O que você está vestindo hoje?
items.note: Use "am/is/are wearing" for present description. "Have on" is also common. Include details: color, type, fit.

items.english: She wears a nice belt with her dresses.
items.portuguese: Ela usa um cinto bonito com seus vestidos.
items.note: Accessories follow normal noun rules. "Wear" can be used for most accessories (wear a watch, wear jewelry).

items.english: I wake up at 6 o'clock every morning.
items.portuguese: Acordo às 6 horas toda manhã.
items.note: Morning routines use present simple. Include specific times with "at" + time (at 6 am, at 7:30 am).

items.english: I have lunch at noon.
items.portuguese: Almoço ao meio-dia.
items.note: Afternoon and evening routines follow the same structure. Use specific times and present simple.

items.english: I always wake up at 6 am.
items.portuguese: Sempre acordo às 6 da manhã.
items.note: Frequency adverbs: always (100%), usually (80%), sometimes (50%), rarely (10%), never (0%). Place after "be" or before main verb.

items.english: On weekdays I work from 9 to 5.
items.portuguese: Nos dias de semana trabalho de 9 a 5.
items.note: Use "on" before day/period: on weekdays, on Monday, on the weekend. Can use present simple for both routines.
items.cue: Dias de Semana vs. Fins de Semana

items.english: First I wake up, then I shower.
items.portuguese: Primeiro acordo, depois tomo um banho.
items.note: Use sequence words: first, then, after that, later, finally. Use time periods: in the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening.

items.english: I have a living room with a big sofa.
items.portuguese: Tenho uma sala de estar com um sofá grande.
items.note: Room names are compound nouns (living room, dining room) or single nouns (bedroom, kitchen, bath). Use "in the" + room.

items.english: I have a comfortable sofa in my living room.
items.portuguese: Tenho um sofá confortável na minha sala.
items.note: Furniture nouns can be countable (a chair, two tables) or uncountable (furniture). Use "have" or "there is/are".

items.english: There is a big kitchen in my house.
items.portuguese: Há uma cozinha grande na minha casa.
items.note: "There is" for singular, "there are" for plural. Negative: "there is not/isn't", "there are not/aren't".

items.english: The refrigerator is in the kitchen.
items.portuguese: O refrigerador fica na cozinha.
items.note: Household items are countable nouns. Use "have", "there is/are", or describe with colors/size.

items.english: My house is small but comfortable.
items.portuguese: Minha casa é pequena mas confortável.
items.note: Combine "there is/are", adjectives, and "have" to give complete house descriptions.

items.english: I have a dog named Max.
items.portuguese: Tenho um cachorro chamado Max.
items.note: Pet names are countable nouns. Use "have" with pets. Describe them with adjectives.

items.english: Lions are strong and powerful.
items.portuguese: Leões são fortes e poderosos.
items.note: Wild animal names are countable. Use present simple to describe their characteristics.

items.english: Dogs are friendly and loyal.
items.portuguese: Cachorros são amigáveis e leais.
items.note: Use adjectives to describe animals. Can use "is" or "are" for physical descriptions.

items.english: The forest is full of animals and plants.
items.portuguese: A floresta é cheia de animais e plantas.
items.note: Nature vocabulary is mostly uncountable or used in singular/plural accordingly.

items.english: What is your favorite animal?
items.portuguese: Qual é seu animal favorito?
items.note: Express preferences: "I like", "I prefer", "My favorite is". Questions: "What is your favorite animal?"

items.english: Happy birthday to you!
items.portuguese: Feliz aniversário para você!
items.note: Birthday expressions use "It is my birthday", "I am turning" + age. "Happy birthday" is an exclamation.

items.english: Christmas is on December 25th.
items.portuguese: Natal é em 25 de dezembro.
items.note: Holiday names are nouns. Use "on" + holiday (on Christmas). Some are always capitalized.

items.english: We are throwing a party tonight.
items.portuguese: Estamos dando uma festa esta noite.
items.note: Party vocabulary uses nouns and verbs: have a party, throw a party, attend a party, celebrate.

items.english: Would you like to come to my party?
items.portuguese: Você gostaria de vir à minha festa?
items.note: Invitations use "Would you like...?", "Can you...?", "I invite you...". Responses: "Yes, I can", "No, I cannot".

items.english: We exchange gifts on Christmas.
items.portuguese: Trocamos presentes no Natal.
items.note: Traditions use present simple or present continuous. "We exchange gifts", "They are celebrating".

beginner-25-review-real-conversations.title: Lição 25: Revisão Iniciante e Conversas Reais
beginner-25-review-real-conversations.skill: Revisar toda a gramática e vocabulário iniciante

items.english: Hi, nice to meet you. What is your name?
items.portuguese: Oi, prazer em conhecê-lo. Como é seu nome?
items.note: Review: verb to be, present simple, questions, personal pronouns, simple sentences with am/is/are.

items.english: Good morning! How are you today?
items.portuguese: Bom dia! Como você está hoje?
items.note: Review: greetings, present simple (how are you), telling time, politeness phrases.

items.english: What do you recommend? The feijoada is very good.
items.portuguese: O que você recomenda? O feijão é muito bom.
items.note: Review: polite requests (I would like), questions (How much?), countable/uncountable nouns, money terms.

items.english: Excuse me, where is the nearest supermarket?
items.portuguese: Com licença, onde fica o supermercado mais próximo?
items.note: Review: directions (left, right, straight), prepositions of place, transportation verbs, polite questions.

items.english: Let me tell you about my day. This morning I woke up at 6 am.
items.portuguese: Deixe-me contar sobre meu dia. Esta manhã acordei às 6 da manhã.
items.note: Review: past simple (had, met, discussed), present continuous, present simple, sequence words.

intermediate-13-past-simple-regular.title: Lição 13: Passado Simples (Verbos Regulares)
intermediate-13-past-simple-regular.skill: Formar o passado simples com verbos regulares (-ed)

items.english: I worked until 6 PM yesterday.
items.portuguese: Eu trabalhei até às 18h ontem.
items.note: Add -ed to the base verb. For verbs ending in -e, add only -d. For verbs ending in consonant + y, change y to i and add -ed.

items.english: I walked (/wɔːkt/) to the office.
items.portuguese: Eu caminhei até o escritório.
items.note: After voiceless sounds (k, p, s, f, sh, ch) = /t/. After voiced sounds = /d/. After t or d = /ɪd/.

items.english: I didnt work yesterday.
items.portuguese: Eu não trabalhei ontem.
items.note: Use "did not" (didn't) + base verb (NOT -ed). The verb returns to base form after "didn't".

items.english: Did you enjoy the party?
items.portuguese: Você gostou da festa?
items.note: Did + subject + base verb. For Wh- questions: Wh-word + did + subject + base verb.

items.english: I started this job last year.
items.portuguese: Eu comecei esse emprego ano passado.
items.note: Common time expressions: yesterday, last (week/month/year), ago, in (year), on (day/date).

intermediate-14-past-simple-irregular.title: Lição 14: Passado Simples (Verbos Irregulares)
intermediate-14-past-simple-irregular.skill: Aprender os 20 verbos irregulares mais comuns

items.english: I was at work all day.
items.portuguese: Eu estava no trabalho o dia todo.
items.note: I/he/she/it WAS. You/we/they WERE. This is the only verb that changes form with different subjects.

items.english: I went to Italy last summer.
items.portuguese: Eu fui para a Itália no verão passado.
items.note: go → went, come → came, see → saw, do → did. Memorize these - they are extremely common!

items.english: I had a meeting this morning.
items.portuguese: Eu tive uma reunião esta manhã.
items.note: have → had, eat → ate, drink → drank, buy → bought. Notice the vowel changes!

items.english: He said he would come later.
items.portuguese: Ele disse que viria mais tarde.
items.note: say → said, tell → told, know → knew, think → thought. "Tell" always needs an object (tell someone).

items.english: I woke up, had breakfast, and went to work.
items.portuguese: Eu acordei, tomei café e fui trabalhar.
items.note: In real stories, you mix regular (-ed) and irregular verbs naturally. Focus on flow, not just rules.

intermediate-15-present-perfect.title: Lição 15: Present Perfect
intermediate-15-present-perfect.skill: Formar o Present Perfect com have/has + particípio passado

items.english: I have finished the project.
items.portuguese: Eu terminei o projeto.
items.note: I/you/we/they HAVE + past participle. He/she/it HAS + past participle. Regular: work → worked. Irregular: go → gone.

items.english: Have you ever traveled alone?
items.portuguese: Você já viajou sozinho?
items.note: EVER in questions (Have you ever...?). NEVER for no experience. ALREADY for completed actions. YET in negatives and questions.

items.english: I have just received your email.
items.portuguese: Eu acabei de receber seu email.
items.note: JUST goes between have/has and the past participle to emphasize that something happened very recently.

items.english: I have studied English for 3 years.
items.portuguese: Eu estudo inglês há 3 anos.
items.note: FOR + period of time (for 2 years, for a week). SINCE + point in time (since 2020, since Monday, since I was a child).

items.english: I have seen that movie. (no specific time)
items.portuguese: Eu vi esse filme. (sem tempo específico)
items.note: Use Present Perfect when time is not specified or when connecting to now. Use Past Simple when the time is specific (yesterday, last week, in 2020).

intermediate-16-future-will-going-to.title: Lição 16: Futuro (Will e Going To)
intermediate-16-future-will-going-to.skill: Usar "will" para previsões e decisões rápidas

items.english: I think she will get the job.
items.portuguese: Eu acho que ela vai conseguir o emprego.
items.note: Will + base verb. Use for predictions, especially with "I think", "probably", "maybe". Negative: will not (wont).

items.english: Ill have a coffee, please.
items.portuguese: Vou querer um café, por favor.
items.note: Use "will" for decisions made at the moment of speaking, offers, and promises.

items.english: Im going to learn Spanish.
items.portuguese: Eu vou aprender espanhol.
items.note: am/is/are + going to + base verb. Use for plans, intentions, and decisions already made.

items.english: Look! The bus is going to leave!
items.portuguese: Olha! O ônibus vai partir!
items.note: Use "going to" when you can see evidence now that something will happen soon.

items.english: Ill see you tomorrow.
items.portuguese: Te vejo amanhã.
items.note: Tomorrow, next (week/month/year), in (time), soon, later, this (evening/weekend), the day after tomorrow.

items.english: I can speak three languages.
items.portuguese: Eu sei falar três idiomas.
items.note: Can + base verb (no "to"). Can doesnt change for he/she. Negative: cannot (cant).

items.english: I could play soccer well when I was 15.
items.portuguese: Eu sabia jogar futebol bem quando tinha 15 anos.
items.note: Could is the past of can for general ability. For a specific achievement, use "was able to".

items.english: I may take a vacation next month.
items.portuguese: Eu talvez tire férias mês que vem.
items.note: May and might express possibility (about 50% certain). Might is slightly less certain than may.

items.english: Could you open the window, please?
items.portuguese: Você poderia abrir a janela, por favor?
items.note: Politeness scale: Can I... < Could I... < May I... "Could" is more polite than "can".

items.english: Can I get you something to drink?
items.portuguese: Posso pegar algo para você beber?
items.note: In conversation, we use modals constantly. The key is matching the right modal to the situation.

items.english: This coffee is hotter than I expected.
items.portuguese: Este café está mais quente do que eu esperava.
items.note: One-syllable adjectives: add -er + than. Two syllables ending in -y: change y to i, add -er.

items.english: This hotel is more comfortable than the last one.
items.portuguese: Este hotel é mais confortável que o último.
items.note: Two or more syllables (not ending in -y): use "more" + adjective + than.

items.english: This is the best pizza in town.
items.portuguese: Esta é a melhor pizza da cidade.
items.note: The + adjective-est. Use for comparing one thing to all others in a group.

items.english: This is the most delicious food Ive ever eaten.
items.portuguese: Esta é a comida mais deliciosa que eu já comi.
items.note: The most + adjective. Use with adjectives of 2+ syllables (not ending in -y).

items.english: This is much better than the original.
items.portuguese: Isso é muito melhor que o original.
items.note: good → better → the best. bad → worse → the worst. far → farther/further → the farthest/furthest.

intermediate-19-conditionals.title: Lição 19: Condicionais (Cláusulas If)
intermediate-19-conditionals.skill: Formar o First Conditional para possibilidades reais

items.english: If the weather is nice, well go to the beach.
items.portuguese: Se o tempo estiver bom, iremos à praia.
items.note: If + present simple, will + base verb. The "if" clause is about a real possibility; the result uses "will".

items.english: If I were you, I would accept the offer.
items.portuguese: Se eu fosse você, aceitaria a oferta.
items.note: If + past simple, would + base verb. Use for imaginary, unlikely, or impossible situations. Use "were" for all subjects with "be".

items.english: What would you do if you lost your job?
items.portuguese: O que você faria se perdesse seu emprego?
items.note: Question word + will/would + subject + verb... if + condition clause.

items.english: Ill go unless its raining.
items.portuguese: Eu vou a menos que esteja chovendo.
items.note: UNLESS = if not. AS LONG AS = only if. IN CASE = for possible situations. PROVIDED THAT = on the condition that.

items.english: If you have time, could you review this?
items.portuguese: Se você tiver tempo, poderia revisar isso?
items.note: Conditionals are very common in polite requests, offers, and everyday planning conversations.

intermediate-20-passive-voice.title: Lição 20: Voz Passiva
intermediate-20-passive-voice.skill: Entender quando usar a voz passiva

items.english: Coffee is grown in Brazil.
items.portuguese: Café é cultivado no Brasil.
items.note: am/is/are + past participle. The object becomes the subject.

items.english: This house was built 100 years ago.
items.portuguese: Esta casa foi construída há 100 anos.
items.note: was/were + past participle. Use for completed actions in the past.

items.english: The winner will be announced tonight.
items.portuguese: O vencedor será anunciado esta noite.
items.note: will be + past participle. Use for future passive actions.

items.english: The telephone was invented by Alexander Graham Bell.
items.portuguese: O telefone foi inventado por Alexander Graham Bell.
items.note: Add "by + agent" when the doer is important or interesting. Omit "by" when the doer is unknown, obvious, or unimportant.

items.english: It is believed that exercise is good for health.
items.portuguese: Acredita-se que exercício é bom para a saúde.
items.note: Use passive when: 1) The doer is unknown, 2) The action is more important, 3) In formal/academic writing, 4) To avoid blame.

items.english: I wake up early every day.
items.portuguese: Eu acordo cedo todos os dias.
items.note: Phrasal verbs combine a verb + particle to create new meaning. "Turn on" ≠ "turn" + "on".
items.cue: Phrasal Verbs do Dia a Dia

items.english: Please come in and sit down.
items.portuguese: Por favor, entre e sente-se.
items.note: Many movement phrasal verbs describe direction or position changes.

items.english: I cant figure out this problem.
items.portuguese: Não consigo resolver este problema.
items.note: Many phrasal verbs relate to problem-solving, completing tasks, and persistence.
items.cue: Phrasal Verbs de Trabalho e Estudo

items.english: I get along well with my colleagues.
items.portuguese: Eu me dou bem com meus colegas.
items.note: These phrasal verbs describe interpersonal relationships and caring for others.

items.english: Turn the light off / Turn off the light.
items.portuguese: Desligue a luz.
items.note: Separable: the object can go between verb and particle. Inseparable: the object must come after the phrasal verb.

items.english: "Im hungry." → She said she was hungry.
items.portuguese: "Estou com fome." → Ela disse que estava com fome.
items.note: Direct: "I am tired." → Reported: She said (that) she was tired. The tense shifts back.

items.english: "I love pizza." → She said she loved pizza.
items.portuguese: "Eu amo pizza." → Ela disse que amava pizza.
items.note: Present Simple → Past Simple. Present Perfect → Past Perfect. Will → Would. Can → Could.

items.english: "Are you coming?" → She asked if I was coming.
items.portuguese: "Você vem?" → Ela perguntou se eu vinha.
items.note: Yes/No questions: asked + if/whether. Wh- questions: asked + wh-word. No inversion in reported questions!

items.english: "Wait here." → She told me to wait there.
items.portuguese: "Espere aqui." → Ela me disse para esperar lá.
items.note: told/asked/ordered + object + (not) to + infinitive. "Dont wait" → She told me not to wait.

items.english: "Im leaving today." → He said he was leaving that day.
items.portuguese: "Estou saindo hoje." → Ele disse que estava saindo naquele dia.
items.note: Time/place words change: today → that day, now → then, here → there, this → that, yesterday → the day before.

intermediate-23-job-interview.title: Lição 23: Habilidades de Entrevista de Emprego

items.english: Im a marketing professional with 3 years of experience in digital advertising.
items.portuguese: Sou um profissional de marketing com 3 anos de experiência em publicidade digital.
items.note: Structure: Present role + Years of experience + Key skills + Career goal.

items.english: My biggest strength is my ability to communicate clearly.
items.portuguese: Meu maior ponto forte é minha capacidade de me comunicar claramente.
items.note: For strengths: be specific with examples. For weaknesses: show self-awareness and improvement.

items.english: I was responsible for managing client relationships.
items.portuguese: Eu era responsável por gerenciar relacionamentos com clientes.
items.note: Use past simple for completed actions. Include quantifiable achievements (numbers, percentages).

items.english: Ive followed your companys work in sustainability.
items.portuguese: Tenho acompanhado o trabalho da empresa em sustentabilidade.
items.note: Research the company! Mention specific things: products, values, recent news, culture.

items.english: What qualities are you looking for in an ideal candidate?
items.portuguese: Que qualidades vocês procuram em um candidato ideal?
items.note: Always have 2-3 questions ready. Show genuine interest in the role and company.

intermediate-24-advanced-travel.title: Lição 24: Inglês Avançado para Viagens
intermediate-24-advanced-travel.skill: Lidar com problemas e reclamações de viagem

items.english: My suitcase didnt arrive. Can you help me track it?
items.portuguese: Minha mala não chegou. Pode me ajudar a rastreá-la?
items.note: Stay calm and polite but assertive. Use "I would like to..." and "Could you please..."

items.english: Help! I need a doctor!
items.portuguese: Socorro! Preciso de um médico!
items.note: Use imperative for urgency. Be clear and direct in emergencies.

items.english: In Brazil, we usually greet with a kiss on the cheek.
items.portuguese: No Brasil, geralmente cumprimentamos com um beijo no rosto.
items.note: Use comparative structures to discuss cultural differences respectfully.

items.english: Would you be able to offer a discount?
items.portuguese: Você poderia oferecer um desconto?
items.note: Use conditional forms for polite negotiation. "Would you be able to..." "Could you possibly..."

items.english: What hidden gems would you recommend?
items.portuguese: Quais lugares secretos você recomendaria?
items.note: Ask open-ended questions to encourage longer responses and deeper conversations.

intermediate-25-present-perfect-continuo.title: Lição 25: Present Perfect Continuous
intermediate-25-present-perfect-continuo.skill: Formar frases no present perfect continuous com have/has been + -ing

items.english: I have been working on this project for three months.
items.portuguese: Tenho trabalhado neste projeto por três meses.
items.note: Present perfect continuous is formed with have/has + been + present participle (-ing form). Subject + have/has + been + verb-ing + for/since + time.

items.english: I have been learning Portuguese for six months.
items.portuguese: Tenho aprendido português por seis meses.
items.note: Use "for" followed by a period of time (hours, days, years). Use "since" followed by a specific point in time (date, day, year, or event). Both show how long an action has been happening.

items.english: I have completed my homework. (result)
items.portuguese: Terminei meu dever de casa. (resultado)
items.note: Present perfect emphasizes the completion of an action (result). Present perfect continuous emphasizes the duration and ongoing nature of an action. Use continuous to show effort, activity, or process
items.cue: Present Perfect vs. Present Perfect Continuous

items.english: I have been teaching English for twelve years.
items.portuguese: Tenho ensinado inglês por doze anos.
items.note: Use present perfect continuous to discuss ongoing activities, professional projects, personal development, and situations that started before now and continue. Often shows visible effects or tiredness

items.english: Have you been waiting long?
items.portuguese: Você está esperando há muito tempo?
items.note: Questions: Have/Has + subject + been + -ing? Negatives: Subject + have/has + not + been + -ing. Contractions: haven't been, hasn't been. Use in natural questioning about duration and ongoing activitie

intermediate-26-relative-pronouns.title: Lição 26: Pronomes Relativos
intermediate-26-relative-pronouns.skill: Identificar e usar pronomes relativos corretamente (who, which, that, where, whose)

items.english: The teacher who works here is very experienced.
items.portuguese: O professor que trabalha aqui é muito experiente.
items.note: "Who" refers to people. "Which" refers to things (non-human). "That" can refer to both people and things, especially in defining clauses. All three connect a relative clause to a noun.

items.english: The city where I grew up is beautiful in spring.
items.portuguese: A cidade onde cresci é linda na primavera.
items.note: "Where" is used for locations and places. It replaces prepositional phrases like "in which" or "at which." "Whose" shows possession and ownership, answering the question "whose is it?"

items.english: The laptop that has the broken screen is being repaired.
items.portuguese: O laptop que tem a tela quebrada está sendo reparado.
items.note: Defining clauses give essential information to identify the noun; no commas used. Non-defining clauses add extra information; commas are required. Example: "The book that is on the table" (defining) v

items.english: The manager whose team won the award works in the department that I lead.
items.portuguese: O gerente cujo time ganhou o prêmio trabalha no departamento que dirijo.
items.note: You can combine multiple relative clauses in one sentence to provide detailed information. Ensure clarity by using appropriate punctuation and pronouns. Keep sentences readable by avoiding excessive n
items.cue: Frases Complexas com Múltiplas Orações Relativas

items.english: Who was the person that you were talking to?
items.portuguese: Quem era a pessoa com quem você estava falando?
items.note: In formal or written English, you can use "which," "who," and "that" in questions and relative clauses. Formal writing often prefers "which" over "that" for non-defining clauses. Professional communic
items.cue: Pronomes Relativos em Perguntas e Escrita Formal

intermediate-27-gerunds-infinitives.skill: Distinguir entre gerúndios e infinitivos e suas funções

items.english: Swimming is my favorite exercise.
items.portuguese: Nadar é meu exercício favorito.
items.note: Gerunds are the -ing form of verbs used as nouns. They can function as subjects ("Running is healthy"), objects ("I enjoy reading"), or objects of prepositions ("before leaving"). Gerunds refer to act

items.english: I enjoy cooking Brazilian dishes.
items.portuguese: Gosto de cozinhar pratos brasileiros.
items.note: Many verbs naturally take gerunds as their objects. Common ones include: enjoy, avoid, consider, finish, practice, suggest, admit, deny, risk, delay, postpone, and keep. The pattern is: verb + gerund

items.english: To improve your English, you must practice daily.
items.portuguese: Para melhorar seu inglês, você deve praticar diariamente.

items.english: I want to learn Portuguese fluently.
items.portuguese: Quero aprender português fluentemente.
items.note: Many verbs take infinitive objects. Common verbs include: want, need, plan, decide, choose, hope, attempt, fail, manage, forget, remember, promise, offer, and refuse. The pattern is: verb + to + base

items.english: I stopped smoking two years ago.
items.portuguese: Parei de fumar há dois anos.

advanced-25-advanced-conditionals.title: Lição 25: Condicionais Avançados
advanced-25-advanced-conditionals.skill: Formar e usar o Third Conditional naturalmente

items.english: If I had known about the sale, I would have bought it.
items.portuguese: Se eu soubesse da promoção, teria comprado.
items.note: If + had + past participle, would/could/might + have + past participle. Used for unreal past situations.

items.english: I wish I had started learning English earlier.
items.portuguese: Eu gostaria de ter começado a aprender inglês mais cedo.
items.note: "I wish I had..." and "If only I had..." express strong regret about the past. "Should have" expresses what was the right thing to do.

items.english: If I had moved to the US, I would speak English fluently now.
items.portuguese: Se eu tivesse me mudado para os EUA, falaria inglês fluentemente agora.
items.note: If + past perfect, would + base verb (present result). The IF clause is about the past, but the result is about NOW.

items.english: If I were braver, I would have spoken up at the meeting.
items.portuguese: Se eu fosse mais corajoso, teria falado na reunião.
items.note: If + past simple (present meaning), would have + past participle (past result). The IF clause is about a permanent trait, the result is about a past event.

items.english: If I see her (1st), I will tell her. If I saw her (2nd), I would tell her.
items.portuguese: Se eu a vir (1st), direi a ela. Se eu a visse (2nd), diria a ela.
items.note: Choose based on reality and time: Zero = facts, 1st = real future possibility, 2nd = unreal present/future, 3rd = unreal past, Mixed = combining times.

advanced-26-relative-clauses.title: Lição 26: Orações Relativas
advanced-26-relative-clauses.skill: Distinguir orações relativas restritivas de explicativas

items.english: The woman who lives next door is a doctor.
items.portuguese: A mulher que mora ao lado é médica.
items.note: Defining clauses identify WHICH person/thing we mean. No commas. You can use "that" instead of "who/which".

items.english: My manager, who has 20 years of experience, approved the project.
items.portuguese: Meu gerente, que tem 20 anos de experiência, aprovou o projeto.
items.note: Non-defining clauses add EXTRA information about something already identified. Use commas. CANNOT use "that" — only who/which/whose/where.

items.english: Thats the colleague whose idea saved the project.
items.portuguese: Esse é o colega cuja ideia salvou o projeto.
items.note: "Whose" shows possession. It replaces his/her/their/its in relative clauses. Works for people AND things.

items.english: The people waiting in line looked impatient. (= who were waiting)
items.portuguese: As pessoas esperando na fila pareciam impacientes.
items.note: Remove who/which/that + be verb. Active: use -ing (the woman speaking). Passive: use past participle (the report written).

items.english: The project that we started last year, which was funded by investors, is almost complete.
items.portuguese: O projeto que começamos ano passado, que foi financiado por investidores, está quase completo.
items.note: Practice combining defining and non-defining clauses in natural speech. Pay attention to comma placement and pronoun choice.

advanced-27-advanced-tenses.title: Lição 27: Tempos Verbais Avançados
advanced-27-advanced-tenses.skill: Usar o Present Perfect Continuous para ações contínuas

items.english: I have been learning Portuguese for six months.
items.portuguese: Estou aprendendo português há seis meses.
items.note: have/has + been + verb-ing. Emphasizes DURATION of an ongoing action. Often with "for" (period) and "since" (starting point).

items.english: I had been driving for five hours when I finally stopped to rest.
items.portuguese: Eu estava dirigindo há cinco horas quando finalmente parei para descansar.
items.note: had + been + verb-ing. For actions that were ongoing BEFORE another past action. Shows duration up to a past point.

items.english: By December, I will have saved enough for a trip.
items.portuguese: Até dezembro, terei economizado o suficiente para uma viagem.
items.note: will + have + past participle. For actions that WILL BE COMPLETED by a specific future time. Key phrase: "by + future time".

items.english: Next week, I will have been studying English for exactly one year.
items.portuguese: Na próxima semana, estarei estudando inglês há exatamente um ano.
items.note: will + have + been + verb-ing. Emphasizes the DURATION of an ongoing action up to a future point.

items.english: I have read 3 books. (result) vs I have been reading a lot. (activity)
items.portuguese: Eu li 3 livros. (resultado) vs Eu tenho lido muito. (atividade)
items.note: Perfect = result/completion. Perfect Continuous = duration/process. Choose based on whether you want to emphasize the result or the ongoing nature of the action.

advanced-28-formal-register.title: Lição 28: Registro Formal
advanced-28-formal-register.skill: Identificar a diferença entre registro formal e informal

items.english: Informal: "Can you help me out?" → Formal: "Would you be able to assist me?"
items.portuguese: Informal: "Pode me ajudar?" → Formal: "Seria possível me auxiliar?"
items.note: Formal English avoids contractions, slang, and phrasal verbs. It uses complete sentences, passive voice, and Latin-origin words.

items.english: The project was successful. Furthermore, it was completed under budget.
items.portuguese: O projeto foi bem-sucedido. Além disso, foi concluído abaixo do orçamento.
items.note: Formal connectors organize ideas clearly: Addition (Furthermore, Moreover), Contrast (Nevertheless, However), Result (Consequently, Therefore), Reference (With regard to, Concerning).

items.english: Dear Mr. Silva, I am writing to follow up on our previous conversation.
items.portuguese: Caro Sr. Silva, estou escrevendo para dar continuidade à nossa conversa anterior.
items.note: Professional emails have clear structure: greeting, purpose, body, closing. Use formal phrases and avoid abbreviations.

items.english: It would appear that there has been a misunderstanding.
items.portuguese: Parece que houve um mal-entendido.
items.note: Hedging makes statements less direct and more polite. Use: seem, appear, tend, might, could, would, perhaps, somewhat, slightly.

items.english: I would like to begin by outlining our main objectives.
items.portuguese: Gostaria de começar delineando nossos principais objetivos.
items.note: Structure: Introduction (I would like to present...), Signposting (Firstly, Moving on to...), Evidence (The data shows...), Conclusion (In summary, To conclude...).

advanced-29-idiomatic-english.title: Lição 29: Inglês Idiomático
advanced-29-idiomatic-english.skill: Entender e usar 20+ expressões idiomáticas comuns

items.english: Could you keep an eye on my bag while I go to the restroom?
items.portuguese: Você pode ficar de olho na minha bolsa enquanto eu vou ao banheiro?
items.note: Idioms are fixed expressions — the words cannot be changed or rearranged. Learn them as complete units, not word by word.

items.english: Lets get the ball rolling on this project.
items.portuguese: Vamos dar início a este projeto.
items.note: Business idioms are very common in meetings and emails. Using them naturally shows fluency and cultural awareness.

items.english: We need to make a decision by tomorrow. (NOT do a decision)
items.portuguese: Precisamos tomar uma decisão até amanhã.
items.note: Collocations are words that naturally go together. Using the right combination sounds natural; the wrong one sounds off. Learn collocations as pairs.

items.english: She was over the moon when she got the promotion.
items.portuguese: Ela ficou nas nuvens quando conseguiu a promoção.
items.note: Emotional idioms add color and naturalness to speech. They show fluency and help you express feelings more vividly than simple adjectives.

items.english: In a nutshell, the project was a success but it took longer than expected.
items.portuguese: Resumindo, o projeto foi um sucesso mas levou mais tempo que o esperado.
items.note: Dont overuse idioms — one or two per conversation sounds natural. Too many sounds forced. Match the idiom to the formality of the situation.

advanced-30-debate-opinion.title: Lição 30: Debate e Opinião
advanced-30-debate-opinion.skill: Expressar opiniões com diferentes graus de intensidade

items.english: In my opinion, remote work increases productivity.
items.portuguese: Na minha opinião, trabalho remoto aumenta a produtividade.
items.note: Mild: "I think...", "It seems to me...". Medium: "I believe...", "In my view...". Strong: "I strongly believe...", "I am convinced that...".

items.english: I couldnt agree more — technology is transforming education.
items.portuguese: Concordo plenamente — tecnologia está transformando a educação.
items.note: Agree: "Absolutely!", "I couldnt agree more", "Thats a great point". Disagree politely: "I see your point, but...", "I respectfully disagree", "Thats one way to look at it, however...".

items.english: Research shows that bilingual people have better cognitive flexibility.
items.portuguese: Pesquisas mostram que pessoas bilíngues têm melhor flexibilidade cognitiva.
items.note: Strong arguments have: 1) A clear position, 2) Evidence (data, examples, expert opinion), 3) Logical reasoning, 4) Acknowledgment of counterarguments.

items.english: Admittedly, AI has some risks. However, the benefits far outweigh them.
items.portuguese: Reconhecidamente, IA tem alguns riscos. No entanto, os benefícios superam em muito.
items.note: Concede first, then counter: "While X is true, Y is more important." This shows you are open-minded but still have a strong position.

items.english: Let me start by stating that I am in favor of renewable energy.
items.portuguese: Deixe-me começar dizendo que sou a favor da energia renovável.
items.note: Debate structure: 1) State position, 2) Give reasons + evidence, 3) Address counterarguments, 4) Restate position with conclusion.

items.english: I was having dinner when suddenly the lights went out.
items.portuguese: Eu estava jantando quando de repente as luzes apagaram.
items.note: Past Simple = main events. Past Continuous = background/setting. Past Perfect = earlier event (before the main story). Combine them for rich narratives.

items.english: The old library was eerily quiet, with dust floating in the golden light.
items.portuguese: A velha biblioteca estava assustadoramente silenciosa, com poeira flutuando na luz dourada.
items.note: Use sensory details: sight, sound, smell, touch, taste. Combine adjectives with adverbs for richer descriptions: "absolutely stunning", "eerily quiet".

items.english: It all started on a rainy Tuesday morning in November.
items.portuguese: Tudo começou numa manhã chuvosa de terça-feira em novembro.
items.note: Good stories have: 1) Setting (where, when), 2) Characters, 3) Complication (what went wrong), 4) Climax (turning point), 5) Resolution (how it ended).

items.english: "I cant believe this is happening," she whispered, her eyes wide with shock.
items.portuguese: "Não acredito que isso está acontecendo," ela sussurrou, com os olhos arregalados de choque.
items.note: Direct speech adds drama: "Stop!" he yelled. Indirect speech is smoother: He told me to stop. Mix both for natural storytelling.

items.english: You wont believe what happened next — the CEO walked in!
items.portuguese: Você não vai acreditar no que aconteceu depois — o CEO entrou!
items.note: Engage listeners with: rhetorical questions ("Can you guess?"), suspense ("Little did I know..."), dramatic pauses, and strong endings.

advanced-32-nuances.title: Lição 32: Nuances do Inglês
advanced-32-nuances.skill: Distinguir palavras comumente confundidas (affect/effect, lay/lie, etc.)

items.english: The weather affected (verb) our plans. The effect (noun) was disappointing.
items.portuguese: O clima afetou (verbo) nossos planos. O efeito (substantivo) foi decepcionante.
items.note: Many confusing word pairs follow patterns: verb ending in -ise/-ize vs noun ending in -ice/-ce (advise/advice, practice/practise). Learn the part of speech to choose correctly.

items.english: There are fewer cars on the road today. (countable)
items.portuguese: Há menos carros na estrada hoje. (contável)
items.note: Countable → fewer, many, a few, each. Uncountable → less, much, a little. "Each" = individual focus. "Every" = group/all focus.

items.english: It depends on the weather. (NOT "depends of")
items.portuguese: Depende do clima. (NOT "depends of")
items.note: Many English prepositions dont match Portuguese translations. Learn verb + preposition as a unit: interested IN, depend ON, good AT, married TO, consist OF.

items.english: She said (that) she was tired. (NOT "she said me")
items.portuguese: Ela disse que estava cansada.
items.note: SAY + words/sentences (no indirect object needed). TELL + person + information (indirect object required). SPEAK = formal, languages. TALK = informal, conversations.

items.english: I am 30 years old. (NOT "I have 30 years")
items.portuguese: Tenho 30 anos. (Em inglês: I AM 30)
items.note: Common Brazilian mistakes: age (have → be), false friends (pretend ≠ pretender), word order in questions, missing "it" as subject (It is raining, NOT Is raining).

advanced-33-business-english.title: Lição 33: Inglês para Negócios
advanced-33-business-english.skill: Liderar e participar de reuniões profissionais

items.english: Thank you all for joining. Lets get started — the agenda is on your screens.
items.portuguese: Obrigado a todos por participarem. Vamos começar — a pauta está nas telas de vocês.
items.note: Meeting language: Opening (The purpose/objective of this meeting...), Agenda management (Moving on..., Lets get back to...), Closing (To summarize..., The next steps are...).

items.english: We would like to propose a revised timeline that accommodates both parties.
items.portuguese: Gostaríamos de propor um cronograma revisado que acomode ambas as partes.
items.note: Negotiation uses conditional and hedging: "We would be willing to..." "If you could meet us halfway..." "Perhaps we could consider..."

items.english: Good morning, everyone. Today I would like to present our quarterly results.
items.portuguese: Bom dia a todos. Hoje gostaria de apresentar nossos resultados trimestrais.
items.note: Signpost language guides the audience: "Firstly... Secondly... Finally...", "Moving on to...", "This leads us to...", "To conclude..."

items.english: I am writing to follow up on the proposal we discussed last Tuesday.
items.portuguese: Escrevo para dar continuidade à proposta que discutimos terça passada.
items.note: Email structure: Subject line (clear + concise), Greeting (Dear...), Purpose (first sentence), Body (details), Action needed (clear request), Closing (professional sign-off).

items.english: I want to make sure we are on the same page regarding the timeline.
items.portuguese: Quero garantir que estamos alinhados em relação ao cronograma.
items.note: Cross-cultural tips: Be explicit (avoid assumptions), use clear language (avoid idioms with unfamiliar audiences), and show respect for different communication styles.

advanced-34-academic-english.title: Lição 34: Inglês Acadêmico
advanced-34-academic-english.skill: Escrever declarações de tese e frases-tema claras

items.english: This essay argues that social media has fundamentally altered political discourse.
items.portuguese: Este ensaio argumenta que a mídia social alterou fundamentalmente o discurso político.
